A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AVATAR and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component and reward ablations, training curves, qualitative examples, and appendix experiments with a 3B model.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds Ola-7B experiments, further ablations, and analyses of reasoning positions, sequence length, and replay-buffer capacity.

M1.justification: The reported VCRS operation changes materially. V1 describes a multiplicative advantage factor using the last 20 processed instances; v2 Section 4.4 and Algorithm 1 instead subtract the historical reward baseline in off-policy advantage estimation and update its history from new on-policy instances. This revises a central learning component, although the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The training datasets and twelve evaluation benchmarks are retained. Applying AVATAR to Ola-7B, analyzing existing SFT samples, and stratifying existing benchmarks by reasoning length do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds inverse-parabolic weighting to the existing advantage-shaping comparison in Table 5. It also reports TOMATO comparisons for Ola-7B and AV-Reasoner, whose corresponding entries were missing in v1 Table 2. The other established benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation of AVATAR on Ola-7B, SFT-present/absent controls, reasoning-length groups, TAS-strength and buffer-capacity sweeps, and GPT-4o analysis of 50,000 SFT examples. Efficiency is now explicitly assessed using generated-completion counts. These expand experimental design; newly disclosed LoRA and default hyperparameters alone do not establish changes to retained experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test inverse-parabolic weighting, dependence on SFT, gains across reasoning lengths, critical-step positions, per-token loss allocation, TAS strength, and replay-buffer capacity. These directly investigate AVATAR's mechanism and sensitivity. The WorldSense ablation, reward ablation, 3B experiments, and qualitative examples already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: V1's primary comparisons report point estimates only. V2 Tables 2–3 introduce 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for baseline-to-AVATAR gains, specifying 10,000 percentile-bootstrap iterations and a 0.05 significance criterion. Neither version specifies repeated-training-run or seed counts; bootstrap iterations are not additional training runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results while retaining the original Qwen-AVATAR benchmark scores. Newly reported Ola-AVATAR scores include 55.7 on DailyOmni and 45.4 on MVBench; TOMATO entries of 25.3 for Ola and 24.9 for AV-Reasoner replace missing entries. New ablation findings accompany these additions. Figure 4 and its account replace v1's 0.75 reward at 2,500 iterations with 0.80 accuracy at 400 iterations and completion-based accounting, rather than establishing a controlled cross-version performance gain.

T1.justification: V2 introduces Equation 11, formally defining off-policy advantages through historical-reward subtraction and off-policy-batch standard deviation, replacing v1's multiplicative VCRS description. The remaining core equations are substantially retained. No new theorem or proof is supplied; the new TAS justification is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary replace the claim of over 35% higher sample efficiency with 5× efficiency and 80% fewer generated completions to reach target performance. This substantially strengthens and changes the accounting of a headline contribution. The stated benchmark improvements and central replay-plus-TAS contribution remain.

C2.justification: V2 develops TAS from an intuitive positional weighting scheme into a claimed data-driven approximation to critical-step importance learned through SFT. It adds interpretations concerning SFT's role in stable grounding, stronger benefits for long reasoning sequences, excessive TAS weighting, and the diversity-versus-staleness tradeoff in buffer capacity. These are substantive mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies a 10k replay buffer and quantile-based tiers, LoRA target modules and parameters, TAS/off-policy/KL coefficients, weighted stage rewards, and majority-vote tie-breaking. It also provides the GPT-4o analysis prompt. These materially improve implementation disclosure without establishing that previously unspecified settings changed. V1's eight-NVIDIA-L40S hardware disclosure is removed; the project link and TAS pseudocode remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds GRPO-λ and CAPO to the credit-assignment discussion, veRL/HybridFlow to replay positioning, and citations supporting newly documented tools and analyses. It removes Mroueh et al.'s off-policy GRPO reference. The broader research positioning remains similar; publication-metadata updates do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the GRPO-limitations, replay, TAS, implementation, and results discussions are rewritten or expanded. VCRS receives a dedicated subsection, experiments are organized into numbered research questions, and the appendix is reorganized around a larger sequence of analyses. These narrative changes extend beyond numbering and newly added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 restructures the main comparison tables around backbone-specific AVATAR applications, adds confidence-interval displays and colored gains, removes reasoning-indicator columns, and broadly restyles tables and captions. It replaces Figure 4, adds several analytical figures and configuration/SFT tables, and relocates the WorldSense table to the appendix. Existing training curves, prompts, and qualitative examples are also reformatted or moved.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1, the additional backbone evaluation, targeted ablations, bootstrap intervals, and implementation settings improve empirical support and transparency. The gains are limited by unresolved consistency problems: v2 Table 1's Stage 3 rewards disagree with Figure 3 and the cumulative recipe in Table 8, while Figure 11's IntentBench results contradict the claim that every benchmark peaks at a 10k buffer. The added evidence is useful, but some stronger interpretations exceed what the displayed results support.
